newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, yen up.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures end mostly lower, yen up.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures ended moderately lower as the dollar remained at highs against the mark.
September marks and Swiss francs posted fresh contract lows during the day and the dollar embarked on a 93-month high against the German unit.
"It seemed pretty well dollar supportive with the move above 1.86 in the cash," an IMM currency desk manager said.
September yen closed higher on the day, but in the middle of the day's range.
Traders said a commission house sold 1,000 September yen on the close, pulling it from $0.008506 to $0.008499.
Traders said a French bank affiliate sold 2,500 marks late in the day after selling 1,500 near midday.
A Swiss bank was said to have sold 1,000 September marks early and slowly bought them back thorughout the day.
Traders said activity petered out in most currencies in choppy afternoon trade, but marks volume was moderate. Traders estimated 40,000 September contracts exchanged hands Friday.
"Marks were the one bright star in the volume category," an IMM trader said.
A flood of U.S. data Friday kept the mood jittery.
Currencies initially expanded opening losses after stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs data, but yen staged a recovery as marks hit new lows.

July jobs rose 316,000 versus average forecasts for a 193,000-job increase. June's original 217,000 payrolls increase was revised upward to 228,000. July's jobless rate fell to 4.8 percent from 5.0 percent in June and against forecasts for 4.9 percent. Average hourly earnings stayed flat at $12.23 versus a forecasts for a 0.2-percent rise.
Next was National Association of Purchasing Management.
Currencies cut their losses slightly after the strong NAPM report shoved stocks and bonds sharply lower.
NAPM rose to 58.6 in July from 55.7 in June. The prices-paid component rose to 53.6 from 48.1 in June.

At the close, September yen rose $0.000017 to $0.008498, marks lost $0.0070 to $0.5380, Swiss francs fell $0.0057 to $0.6581, sterling lost $0.0088 to $1.6284, Canadian dollar lost $0.0013 to $0.7262, Aussie dollar lost $0.0075 to $0.7392, and Mexican peso fell $0.000375 to $0.125225.
